name: Chikanda (Zambian Orchid Sausage)
author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors

ingredients.item: 2 cups water (for boiling the chikanda roots)
1 cup dried and ground wild orchid tubers (chikanda roots)
½ cup water (for mixing with the groundnuts)

steps: In a pot, bring 2 cups of water to a boil. Add the dried and ground chikanda roots to the boiling water. Boil for about 30 minutes to soften them.
While the chikanda roots are boiling, toast the groundnuts in a dry pan over medium heat until they are slightly browned and aromatic.
Allow the boiled chikanda roots and the roasted groundnuts to cool down to room temperature.
In a blender or food processor, grind the roasted groundnuts into a fine powder. Add ½ cup of water to the groundnuts and blend to form a smooth paste.
In the same blender or food processor, blend the cooked rice until it becomes a smooth paste.
In a large bowl, mix together the ground chikanda, groundnut paste, and rice paste. Use your hands or a wooden spoon to combine the ingredients thoroughly.
Add the chopped onion, minced garlic, and chopped hot pepper (if using) to the mixture. Mix well.
Season the chikanda mixture with ground cayenne pepper, ground cumin, and salt to taste. Adjust the seasoning according to your preference.
Take a handful of the chikanda mixture and roll it into a sausage shape using your hands.
Repeat the process until all the mixture is used up, forming several chikanda sausages.
Place the chikanda sausages on a clean surface or plate and allow them to dry and firm up for about 3 to 4 hours.
Once the chikanda sausages have dried and firmed up, they are ready to be served.

culture.text: Chikanda is a Zambian dish made from the boiled root tubers of terrestrial orchids also called chikanda. The dish is often called "African polony" because it has a texture that resembles bologna. Chikanda can be eaten as a snack, dessert, or an accompaniment to nshima, a maize flour porridge.
